title: Blank cells beyond the elapsed time
statement: Let $M$ be an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, let $O$ be a language over its symbol alphabet, and let $x$ be an input word. After running $M$ relative to $O$ for $t$ steps from its initial configuration on $x$, every cell $z$ of every one of its $k+1$ work tapes is blank whenever $t\le |z|$, where $z$ is an integer position.
hypotheses_covered: An oracle machine $M$ with $k$ ordinary work tapes
An oracle language $O$ over the symbol alphabet
A work-tape index among the $k+1$ tapes
replaced:
Let $M$ be an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, $O$ an oracle
language, $x$ an input word, and $t \in \mathbb{N}$.  Then in the
configuration reached by running $M$ with oracle $O$ for $t$ steps from its
initial configuration on $x$, every work-tape cell at an integer position $z$
with $t \le \abs{z}$ is blank.  In particular, the query tape always contains
a blank cell at a nonnegative position, so the empty-word fallback in the
definition of the query string is never invoked in an initialized run.
